stem:
A frequency polygon for a frequency distribution is drawn by plotting the frequency against the mid-value of each class and joining consecutive points with straight lines. The classes and frequencies are:

Class: 10-20, Frequency: 5
Class: 20-30, Frequency: 12
Class: 30-40, Frequency: 18
Class: 40-50, Frequency: 9
Class: 50-60, Frequency: 6

The frequency polygon must be brought to the x-axis by extending lines to two additional points. What are the mid-values of these two anchor classes?

per_option_rationale.rationale: The polygon is anchored to zero by adding a class just below the first (0-10, mid-value 5) and just above the last (60-70, mid-value 65), both with frequency zero.
Using the lower limit of the first class (10) and upper limit of the last class (60) as anchor points instead of the mid-values of the adjacent fictitious classes.

Using 0 and 70 as anchor x-values by taking the very first lower boundary and the very last upper boundary, but the anchor points should be mid-values of adjacent classes, not boundaries of the existing classes.
Using the mid-values of the first and last actual data classes (15 and 55) rather than the mid-values of the imaginary adjacent classes.

explanation: To close a frequency polygon at both ends, add an imaginary class just before the first class and just after the last class, each with frequency zero. The imaginary first class is 0-10 (mid-value = 5) and the imaginary last class is 60-70 (mid-value = 65). The polygon is anchored at (5, 0) and (65, 0).

explanation_sections.punchline: Frequency polygon closes at mid-values of two adjacent zero-frequency classes: 5 (for class 0-10) and 65 (for class 60-70).
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: frequency polygon construction. Decisive move: identify the anchor classes. First class is 10-20, so the preceding imaginary class is 0-10 with mid-value (0+10)/2 = 5. Last class is 50-60, so the succeeding imaginary class is 60-70 with mid-value (60+70)/2 = 65. Both have frequency 0.
explanation_sections.lesson: A frequency polygon is anchored to the x-axis using the mid-values of hypothetical adjacent classes on both sides, each with zero frequency - never at the actual class boundaries.
explanation_sections.timing: 30 seconds. Identify the two adjacent imaginary classes. Compute their mid-values. Trap: option 2 uses the class limits (10 and 60) instead of mid-values of the imaginary classes.
